issues.failure_explanation: B has i.i.d. Bernoulli(m/N) diagonal entries, so its number of non-zero rows is a single Bin(N, m/N) random variable, not a prescribed size. For one fixed B there are no "the m_i non-zero rows" for each of the K different nested sizes m_1 < ... < m_K, and the realized count is random rather than equal to m_i. Hence the constructed S_i = sqrt(N/m_i) B_i HDP are not the exactly-m_i-row SRHT matrices to which the embedding theorem (thm:bigtheorem, used via Lemma lemma1) applies, so the described procedure does not deliver the objects the theory requires.

failure_location.quote: by sampling the rows of the data \((S_0X, S_0Y)\), namely by left-multiplying the random matrix \(B_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m_i \times N}\), which is consisted of the \(m_i\) non-zero rows of \(B\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the row-extraction description by nested exact-size uniform subsampling: define B_i as selecting exactly m_i of the retained rows (nested across i), or sample S_i directly at size m_i from HDP; then Theorem thm:bigtheorem applies verbatim and all guarantees and cost figures survive.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed efficient construction of the K sketched subproblems (and thus the input of Algorithm Alg-SRHT and the Nd log2 N sketching-cost accounting) is not well defined as written, and the embedding-based guarantees are not attached to the described procedure.
issues.title: Sketched-data construction via 'the m_i non-zero rows of B' is ill-defined
issues.why_classification: A local definitional repair (specify exact-size nested sampling) preserves every guarantee, rate, and complexity claim; no new lemma or construction is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm Alg-SRHT uses a single global counter t and never resets the momentum at subproblem boundaries, so at the first iteration of subproblem i (i >= 2) the term eta(beta_t - beta_{t-1}) uses beta_{t-1} = the (a_{i-1}-1)-th iterate of subproblem i-1. The proof instead analyzes the recursion initialized with the duplicated pair beta_{-1}^i = beta_0^i, which is what makes the initial two-vector norm reduce to sqrt(2)*||X(beta_0^i - beta_tilde^i)||. The recursion actually defined by the algorithm is a different two-step system, so the proved contraction does not apply to the stated algorithm; the missing step is a bound on the carried-over component ||X(beta_{a_{i-1}-1}^{i-1} - beta_tilde^i)||. The same mismatch occurs at the 1st-to-2nd stage transition in Lemma finalerror, Lemma 'M-IHS converging rate', and hence Theorem Thf.

failure_location.quote: In the case \(i > 1\), we set the initial iterates \({\beta_{-1}^{i}} = {\beta_{0}^{i}} = {\beta_{a_{i-1}}^{i-1}}\) based on the iterates from the previous sketched LS subproblem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the reset (set beta_{t-1} := beta_t at the start of each subproblem and of the 2nd stage) to Algorithms Alg-framework/Alg-SRHT, or keep the algorithm and add the short argument bounding the carried-over component by the already-proven contraction and the delta_{i-1} control; the stated bounds then hold with at most constant-factor changes.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantees of Theorems thm:convergence_theorem1 and Thf are established only for a modified iteration with momentum reset at each subproblem/stage, not for Algorithm Alg-SRHT as written; the advertised guarantees for the implemented scheme are unsupported until this gap is closed.
issues.title: Convergence proof analyzes a momentum-reset variant, not Algorithm Alg-SRHT
issues.why_classification: A one-line pseudocode change or a short supplementary bound using already-established estimates resolves it; every substantive claim and guarantee is preserved.

The statement instead defines r = sqrt((m_{i-1} - d)/(m_i - d)) < 1, the reciprocal. With the statement's r the decisive step ((1/3)^{a_i}[(1+omega)r+1]delta_i <= omega*delta_i) does not follow, so counts a_i set at the stated smaller lower bounds do not fulfill (14)/(23). Downstream, Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE uses the statement's formula to conclude a_i < alpha with alpha = log_3{[1+(1+omega)/sqrt2]/omega} and a_2 < ... < a_K; with the corrected ratio these are false: the required counts are larger (a_2 -> infinity as gamma -> 2^{-K}), decrease rather than increase in i, and no uniform alpha exists.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the ratio's direction in Theorem lowerBoundai's statement to sqrt((m_i - d)/(m_{i-1} - d)) as in its proof, and recompute Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE with the corrected, larger, decreasing counts (alpha becomes the i = 2 value, depending on gamma); a comparable complexity statement survives.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised iteration-count guidance of Theorem lowerBoundai does not deliver the precision (14); the alpha-bound, the 'log_3(1/omega) < a_i < alpha' conclusion and the first-stage cost 4*alpha*Nd in Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE, and the claimed increasing sequence a_2 < ... < a_K (main text and Appendix cmpxtyAlgSLSEPrf) are invalid.

issues.why_classification: The repair is contained (one corrected formula plus recomputation of the downstream constants), but a stated quantitative guarantee (the alpha-bound and the monotonicity) is withdrawn, so it exceeds a minor local fix while a comparable result survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The prediction error E||X(beta_T - beta)|| has noise floor equal to the OLS error E||X(beta_hat - beta)||, which the paper itself computes as Delta = ||X(beta_hat - beta)||^2 ~ sigma^2 d, i.e., level ~ sigma*sqrt(d) > sigma for d > 1. Hence 'terminate when the estimator achieves the noise level sigma' is unattainable as written, and the proof's translation '(1/3)^T <= sigma' both drops the initial-error factor E||X(beta_0 - beta)|| (only asserted to be a constant) and uses the wrong scale. The derived T = log_3(1/sigma), the bound T - T^dagger < log_3(omega^K/sigma), the condition omega > sigma^{1/K}, and the listed second-stage cost 4[log_3(omega^K/sigma)]Nd are therefore miscomputed.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper fixes E[.] over the noise zeta only. For fixed sketches, beta_tilde^i - beta = (X^T S_i^T S_i X)^{-1} X^T S_i^T S_i zeta and X(beta_hat - beta) = U_X U_X^T zeta, so E||X(beta_tilde^i - beta)||^2 / E||X(beta_hat - beta)||^2 = tr[(U_X^T S_i^T S_i U_X)^{-1}]/d exactly. Under the paper's own embedding guarantee (Theorem thm:bigtheorem, in force in its regime m_i >= m_1 > r = O(d log d)), this ratio is <= 1/(1-eps) ~ 1.1, contradicting the claimed limit (1-gamma)/(xi-gamma) > 1.1 whenever xi < 1 - eps(1-gamma) (e.g. gamma = 1/8, xi = 1/2 gives 7/3). In the lemma's own regime the correct in-sample limit of this ratio is xi/(xi-gamma), not (1-gamma)/(xi-gamma): the displayed value is the out-of-sample (population) prediction efficiency of Dobriban-Liu, a different functional from the in-sample ratio written in the lemma. Hence the lemma is false as stated, and the finite-N, high-probability bounds built on it (the sqrt((N-d)/(m_i-d)) factors) are unsupported; moreover Remark remarkA7 adds two extra conditions (the xi > m_i/N > d/N > gamma ordering and a variance comparison) that the consuming theorems never assume.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop Lemma lemma:lemma3 and bound the sketched error directly from the paper's own embedding result: E||X(beta_tilde^i - beta)||^2 = sigma^2 tr[(U_X^T S_i^T S_i U_X)^{-1}] <= sigma^2 d/(1-eps), so delta_i <= (1-eps)^{-1/2}(1+o(1)) E||X(beta_hat - beta)||; rerun the proofs of remarkA7, finalerror, Thf, lowerBoundai and cmpxtyAlgSLSE with this constant (the variance conditions of Remark remarkA7 become unnecessary).
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative loss analysis of Sketch-and-Solve (the PE narrative, the sqrt((N-d)/(m_i-d)) factors in Lemma finalerror and Theorem Thf, the delta_i-based stopping criterion, the ratio step in the proof of Theorem lowerBoundai, and the r(i-1,i)/alpha figures of Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE) rests on a false lemma and is unsupported. The headline qualitative guarantees (exponential contraction, OLS-level final precision, initialization-dominated cost) survive, since a stronger in-source bound is available.

issues.why_classification: The false lemma and its PE-based narrative must be replaced, but the replacement is a contained, in-source argument (Neumann bound from Lemma lemma1) that preserves every headline guarantee with comparable constants; no advertised regime or guarantee type is lost.
